question.text: A train moving at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> towards a stationary object emits a sound of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>930</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. Some part of the wave gets reflected from the object, back to the train as an echo. The frequency of this echo, as detected by the driver of the train is [speed of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
The speed of the train, vT=20 m s-1

The speed of sound in air, v=330 m s-1

The frequency of the echo detected by the driver of the train is

v'=vv+vTv-vT

v'=930330+20330-20=930×350310 Hz

⇒v'=1050 Hz
